faq.about.question: What is PPI?
faq.about.answer: The exam protocol interface (PPI) is a platform where students can find past exams, practice exams, and other exam protocols, and share protocols of their own.
faq.account.question: Who can create an account?
faq.account.answer: Accounts are for University of Tübingen students with a zx identifier. You must verify your student email address to activate your account.
faq.access.question: How do I access exam protocols?
faq.access.answer: Sign in and unlock access to a course with tokens. The cost and access period are shown before you unlock it. While access is active, you can view and download published protocols.
faq.upload.question: Which protocols can I upload?
faq.upload.answer: PDF and TXT files up to 30 MiB are accepted. Only upload protocols you are allowed to share, and do not include other people’s personal data.
faq.review.question: What happens after I upload a protocol?
faq.review.answer: The file goes through technical safety and content checks. The student council then reviews the submission. A protocol is published only after approval; if changes are requested, you can submit an improved version.
faq.tokens.question: How can I receive tokens?
faq.tokens.answer: Reviewers may award tokens for eligible contributions. The amount and allocation follow the current settings. Improvements to an existing submission do not receive an additional reward.
faq.report.question: How do I report an inaccurate or problematic protocol?
faq.report.answer: Open the course page and use its report option for errors or problematic content. The student council will review the report.
